facts: The original assembly consisted of the three-story entrance tower between the single-story Kahili Room and a two-story vestibule. The tower has a copper pyramid, gabled front and two sandstone entrance arches. Hawaiian and Pacific halls were later additions. Copper roofs are hipped and Hawaiian Hall’s gables have oculi.
The connected main halls are made of locally quarried Kapālama basalt stone. Pacific Hall was historically named Polynesian Hall.

record: Lead architectural practice for the restoration
facts: The 2006–2013 renovation preserved the historic main building fabric.
